questions.q: What did Goethe do before writing?
a: He smelled rotten apples to get into the mood
He walked for exactly one hour every morning
He read aloud from old letters and diaries
He sharpened a dozen pencils at his desk
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses this example to show that creative rituals can be personal and odd.

questions.q: According to the summary, what does a daily schedule do for creative work?
a: It reserves time for work and keeps work out of free time
It guarantees a steady and predictable income
It removes the need for inspiration or ideas
It makes every creative project shorter
questions.why: Lesson 1 says scheduling sets a time frame and protects your free time.

a: A personal work space or time reserved for undisturbed creativity
A retreat you must rent for at least a month
A notebook for capturing dreams and ideas
A group that meets to critique your work
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes it as a space or time where nothing can interrupt you.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest doing to make your Bliss Station distraction-free?
a: Put your phone on airplane mode
Play music with lyrics at high volume
Invite coworkers to work beside you
Keep notifications on for urgent news
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares airplane mode to a flight with no outside input.

questions.q: What advice does the summary give about monetizing creative work?
a: Stay authentic rather than chase trends for money
Accept every paid project you are offered
Copy whatever format is selling best right now
Keep your art completely separate from any audience
questions.why: Lesson 3 says passion-driven work brings more joy, and gifting your work can help.
